title: Adult PFT Phraseology and Selection Catalog
scope: English-language adult routine PFT reporting, with clearly marked optional adjunct modules. No complete CPET or pediatric interpretation engine.
authorship: All selectable phrases are newly composed examples, not quotations or mandated ATS/ERS report text.

selection_contract.automatic: Eligible only after reliable measurement states and derived facts have been computed under the rule specification. Automatic means offer a draft phrase, not finalize a report.
selection_contract.documented_observation: Requires the exact observation from the technician, laboratory, or clinician; do not infer it from a number.
selection_contract.review: Requires explicit clinician selection or a reviewed contextual fact; do not enable or insert automatically from raw metrics.
selection_contract.missing_fact: Unknown/missing must fail the condition. Never coerce unknown to normal, absent, or false-negative.
selection_contract.placeholders: Check required placeholders for the selected variant. If absent, offer a complete variant without that placeholder or suppress it; never invent a value.
selection_contract.exclusive_group: Selection of a phrase replaces an existing conflicting option in the same group; use the semantic conflict rules for cross-group conflicts.

quality.title: Test quality and limitations
quality.note: Use observed or laboratory-supplied quality findings. Grade FEV1 and FVC separately; report quality for each test component. Quality states must never be inferred from the numerical result alone.

spirometry.title: Individual spirometry metrics
spirometry.note: A metric statement describes the measurement. Physiologic pattern statements use combinations of valid metrics. A low FEV1 is not synonymous with obstruction, and a high FEV1/FVC is not a diagnosis.

patterns.title: Spirometric and ventilatory patterns
patterns.note: Use reliable TLC to confirm restriction and mixed impairment. Preserve component labels when quality is limited. PRISm is a defined phenotype whose thresholds must be declared.

flows.title: Mid-expiratory flow, peak flow, and MVV
flows.note: These measurements are descriptive and cannot independently diagnose small airway disease or respiratory muscle weakness.

loops.title: Flow-volume and volume-time loops
loops.note: All morphology phrases require actual curve review or a documented reviewer observation. Numerical indices cannot establish a loop shape or lesion.

bronchodilator.title: Bronchodilator response
bronchodilator.note: Keep current technical-response criteria distinct from a legacy profile or disease-specific diagnostic criterion. A significant response and normalization of obstruction are separate findings.

volumes.title: Lung volumes and volume distribution
volumes.note: Use volume-specific LLN/ULN and method metadata. Increased RV/TLC can occur because TLC is low; the ratio must be interpreted with absolute volumes.

diffusion.title: DLCO and adjustment status
diffusion.note: Grade gas-transfer impairment using the selected DLCO reference and correction basis. A low DLCO is a physiologic finding, not an imaging or vascular diagnosis.

va_kco.title: VA, KCO, and VA/TLC
va_kco.note: KCO is the transfer coefficient; do not label it DLCO corrected for alveolar volume. A normal KCO cannot normalize a low DLCO, and VA cannot substitute for TLC.

muscle.title: Respiratory muscle testing, supine VC, and cough flow
muscle.note: Interpret pressure magnitudes with method-appropriate references and documented effort. Low volitional pressures raise concern but do not prove neuromuscular weakness. There is no universal ATS/ERS mild/moderate/severe percent-predicted grading for MIP/MEP.

methacholine.title: Methacholine challenge
methacholine.note: Prefer protocol-specific PD20 when delivered dose is known. Preserve dose units and the post-diluent baseline. Severity categories describe airway responsiveness, not asthma severity.

indirect.title: Exercise, EVH, and other indirect challenges
indirect.note: Optional module. Import the actual protocol and laboratory positivity criterion; symptoms alone do not establish exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.

feno.title: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide
feno.note: Optional adult module. FeNO describes a biomarker; low FeNO does not exclude asthma and high FeNO is not an independent asthma diagnosis.

resistance.title: Airway resistance and conductance
resistance.note: Optional module. Apply equipment- and method-specific reference limits. Raw and sGaw do not independently classify or localize disease.

oscillometry.title: Respiratory oscillometry
oscillometry.note: Optional specialist module. Require device, frequency, reference equation, quality, and units. Resistance includes the respiratory system and should not be treated as a direct anatomic measurement of small airways.

washout.title: Multiple-breath washout
washout.note: Optional specialist module. Report actual tracer, device, method, reference, and quality. No universal LCI cutoff is supplied in this package.

walk.title: Walk testing and exertional oxygenation
walk.note: Optional field-test module, distinct from complete CPET. Preserve oxygen device/flow, walking aid, nadir saturation, signal quality, and limiting symptom.

serial.title: Comparison with prior studies
serial.note: Report direction and magnitude separately from clinical importance. Match pre/post-bronchodilator state, method, reference, adjustment basis, and quality. Universal longitudinal significance thresholds are not assumed.

integrated.title: Integrated impression options
integrated.note: These are reusable report assemblies rather than diagnoses. The underlying component findings must be valid. Differential and etiologic interpretation remain review-only.

followup.title: Optional follow-up language
followup.note: Suggestions are offered for clinician selection. They must not automatically create orders, prescribe treatment, or claim a diagnosis.

phrases.label: Acceptable and repeatable

templates.standard: Spirometry meets acceptability and repeatability criteria.
templates.expanded: The spirometry maneuvers meet laboratory acceptability and repeatability criteria; reported values are suitable for interpretation.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Repeatability limitation

templates.standard: Spirometry repeatability criteria were not met.
templates.expanded: Variation between efforts limits confidence in the reported spirometric values and in classification near the reference limits.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Usable, incompletely acceptable

templates.standard: Usable spirometry was obtained, although full acceptability criteria were not met.
templates.expanded: The available maneuvers support a cautious interpretation; technical limitations should be considered when assessing the size of an abnormality.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Uninterpretable spirometry

templates.standard: No interpretable spirometry was obtained.
templates.expanded: The available maneuvers do not support reliable spirometric classification; repeat testing may be appropriate if clinically useful.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Cough affecting FEV1

templates.standard: Cough during the first second affects interpretation of FEV1.
templates.expanded: Cough during the first second compromises FEV1; FVC must be assessed independently for usability.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Early termination

templates.standard: Premature termination may underestimate FVC.
templates.expanded: Early termination limits FVC measurement and may artificially increase FEV1/FVC; apparent ratio preservation should be interpreted cautiously.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Incomplete inspiration

templates.standard: Incomplete inspiration may underestimate measured volumes.
templates.expanded: Failure to start at maximal inspiration may underestimate FEV1 and FVC and can affect the interpretation of the overall pattern.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Suboptimal start

templates.concise: The start of expiration is suboptimal.
templates.standard: A suboptimal start limits assessment of early expiratory flow.
templates.expanded: The initial expiratory effort does not meet laboratory start-of-test criteria; FEV1 and peak flow require caution.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Mouth leak

templates.standard: A leak at the mouthpiece affects measured flows or volumes.
templates.expanded: The observed mouthpiece leak limits the reliability of affected measurements; interpretation should identify which components remain usable.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Glottic closure

templates.standard: The maneuver is interrupted by apparent glottic closure.
templates.expanded: Observed glottic closure limits the affected portion of the maneuver and may make FVC or inspiratory-loop interpretation unreliable.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Variable effort

templates.standard: Effort varies across maneuvers.
templates.expanded: Observed variation in effort limits confidence in measured flows and volumes; the report should distinguish usable values from uninterpretable components.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Fatigue limitation

templates.standard: Fatigue limited completion of the test session.
templates.expanded: The technician documented fatigue during testing, limiting the number or quality of available maneuvers.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Symptom limitation

templates.standard: Testing was limited by {limiting_symptom}.
templates.expanded: The test session was limited by {limiting_symptom}; affected measurements should be interpreted in that context.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Lung-volume quality limitation

templates.standard: Technical limitations reduce confidence in lung-volume measurements.
templates.expanded: Lung-volume quality criteria were not fully met; confirmation of restriction or hyperinflation is limited.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: DLCO quality limitation

templates.standard: Technical limitations reduce confidence in DLCO.
templates.expanded: DLCO maneuver quality is limited, which may affect the reported value and its severity classification.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Single DLCO maneuver

templates.concise: DLCO is based on one maneuver.
templates.standard: Only one usable DLCO maneuver was obtained.
templates.expanded: DLCO is based on a single usable maneuver; within-session repeatability could not be established.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Low inspired volume during DLCO

templates.standard: The DLCO maneuver was performed at a reduced inspired volume.
templates.expanded: Incomplete inspiration during the DLCO maneuver may reduce VA and affect DLCO and KCO interpretation.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Respiratory-pressure quality limitation

templates.standard: Respiratory-pressure measurements have technical or effort limitations.
templates.expanded: Volitional pressure measurements are limited by the documented technique or effort and cannot establish muscle weakness on their own.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

phrases.label: Reported quality grades

templates.standard: Spirometry quality is graded separately: FEV1 {fev1_grade}; FVC {fvc_grade}.
templates.expanded: Laboratory quality grades are FEV1 {fev1_grade} and FVC {fvc_grade}; interpretation should account for the limitations associated with each grade.

notes: Use only when the corresponding limitation or quality status is documented.

templates.standard: FEV1 is within the expected reference range.
templates.expanded: FEV1 is within reference limits for the selected equation; its relationship to other measurements determines the physiologic pattern.

templates.standard: FEV1 is below the lower limit of normal.
templates.expanded: FEV1 is reduced relative to the selected reference equation; this finding alone does not establish its cause.

templates.standard: FEV1 exceeds the upper limit of normal.
templates.expanded: FEV1 is above the reference range; a large measured volume is not, by itself, evidence of obstructive lung disease.

templates.standard: FVC is within the expected reference range.
templates.expanded: FVC is within reference limits for the selected equation; its relationship to other measurements determines the physiologic pattern.

templates.standard: FVC is below the lower limit of normal.
templates.expanded: FVC is reduced relative to the selected reference equation; this finding alone does not establish its cause.

templates.standard: FVC exceeds the upper limit of normal.
templates.expanded: FVC is above the reference range; a large measured volume is not, by itself, evidence of obstructive lung disease.

templates.standard: SVC is within the expected reference range.
templates.expanded: SVC is within reference limits for the selected equation; its relationship to other measurements determines the physiologic pattern.

templates.standard: SVC is below the lower limit of normal.
templates.expanded: SVC is reduced relative to the selected reference equation; this finding alone does not establish its cause.

templates.standard: SVC exceeds the upper limit of normal.
templates.expanded: SVC is above the reference range; a large measured volume is not, by itself, evidence of obstructive lung disease.

templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is below the lower limit of normal.
templates.expanded: A valid FEV1/FVC below the lower limit of normal supports an obstructive ventilatory impairment.

templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is within reference limits.
templates.expanded: FEV1/FVC is within reference limits; this does not by itself establish that all pulmonary function is normal.

templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is above the reference range.
templates.expanded: An increased FEV1/FVC is nonspecific and may accompany a reduced FVC; it does not establish restriction without TLC.

phrases.label: Ratio near LLN

templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is close to the lower reference limit.
templates.expanded: FEV1/FVC lies near the lower reference limit; biological variability, test quality, and clinical context are relevant.

notes: Near-LLN is a configurable review flag, not a separate ATS/ERS category. Retain the actual low/normal state.

phrases.label: Below 0.70, at/above LLN

templates.concise: FEV1/FVC is below 0.70 but preserved by LLN.
templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is below the fixed ratio of 0.70 but is not below its age-adjusted LLN.
templates.expanded: The fixed-ratio and LLN classifications differ; specify the diagnostic framework rather than automatically labeling this as obstruction.

notes: This does not by itself diagnose or exclude COPD.

templates.concise: FEV1/FVC is reduced by LLN despite being at least 0.70.
templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is below the LLN despite remaining at or above 0.70.
templates.expanded: The age-adjusted reference comparison supports obstruction even though the fixed-ratio threshold is not crossed.

phrases.label: SVC exceeds FVC

templates.standard: Slow vital capacity is greater than forced vital capacity.
templates.expanded: A reproducible SVC greater than FVC may reflect dynamic airway closure during forced expiration; technical differences and effort should also be considered.

notes: Do not impose a universal disease-defining difference or replace FEV1/FVC without a configured FEV1/VC reference.

templates.standard: FEV1/SVC is below the configured reference limit.
templates.expanded: A reduced FEV1/SVC may reveal airflow limitation when FEV1/FVC is preserved; interpretation requires an appropriate reference and reproducible vital-capacity maneuvers.

templates.standard: FEV1/FEV6 is {fev1_fev6_state} relative to its own reference range.
templates.expanded: An alternative FEV1/FEV6 ratio is reported using a validated reference; FEV1/FVC cutoffs are not interchangeable with this ratio.

phrases.label: FEV1 mild impairment

templates.standard: The reduction in FEV1 is mild by z-score.
templates.expanded: FEV1 shows mild physiologic impairment using the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: FEV1 is {fev1_L} L ({fev1_pct_pred}% predicted; z-score {fev1_z}), a mild reduction.

notes: This grades the named measurement, not overall disease severity.

phrases.label: FEV1 moderate impairment

templates.standard: The reduction in FEV1 is moderate by z-score.
templates.expanded: FEV1 shows moderate physiologic impairment using the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: FEV1 is {fev1_L} L ({fev1_pct_pred}% predicted; z-score {fev1_z}), a moderate reduction.

notes: This grades the named measurement, not overall disease severity.

phrases.label: FEV1 severe impairment

templates.standard: The reduction in FEV1 is severe by z-score.
templates.expanded: FEV1 shows severe physiologic impairment using the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: FEV1 is {fev1_L} L ({fev1_pct_pred}% predicted; z-score {fev1_z}), a severe reduction.

notes: This grades the named measurement, not overall disease severity.

phrases.label: FVC mild impairment

templates.standard: The reduction in FVC is mild by z-score.
templates.expanded: FVC shows mild physiologic impairment using the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: FVC is {fvc_L} L ({fvc_pct_pred}% predicted; z-score {fvc_z}), a mild reduction.

notes: This grades the named measurement, not overall disease severity.

phrases.label: FVC moderate impairment

templates.standard: The reduction in FVC is moderate by z-score.
templates.expanded: FVC shows moderate physiologic impairment using the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: FVC is {fvc_L} L ({fvc_pct_pred}% predicted; z-score {fvc_z}), a moderate reduction.

notes: This grades the named measurement, not overall disease severity.

phrases.label: FVC severe impairment

templates.standard: The reduction in FVC is severe by z-score.
templates.expanded: FVC shows severe physiologic impairment using the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: FVC is {fvc_L} L ({fvc_pct_pred}% predicted; z-score {fvc_z}), a severe reduction.

notes: This grades the named measurement, not overall disease severity.

templates.standard: FEV1, FVC, and FEV1/FVC are within reference limits.
templates.expanded: Spirometry is within reference limits; lung volumes, gas transfer, and clinical context provide additional information.

templates.standard: Spirometry demonstrates an obstructive ventilatory impairment.
templates.expanded: FEV1/FVC is below the LLN, supporting an obstructive ventilatory impairment.

templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is reduced, with FEV1 remaining within reference limits.
templates.expanded: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is present despite a preserved FEV1; the ratio identifies the pattern, while FEV1 describes the magnitude of impairment.

templates.standard: FVC is reduced with a preserved ratio; lung volumes are required to assess for restriction.
templates.expanded: The low FVC with preserved FEV1/FVC suggests a possible restrictive pattern, but TLC is needed to distinguish restriction from other causes of reduced vital capacity.

templates.standard: FEV1 and/or FVC are reduced with a preserved FEV1/FVC and normal TLC.
templates.expanded: Reduced spirometric volumes with a preserved ratio and TLC within reference limits constitute a nonspecific pattern; the cause requires clinical correlation.

templates.standard: TLC is below the LLN, confirming a restrictive ventilatory impairment.
templates.expanded: A reduced TLC confirms restriction; spirometry and gas-transfer findings help characterize the associated physiology.

templates.standard: TLC is reduced without disproportionate elevation of residual-volume fractions.
templates.expanded: The lung-volume distribution is consistent with a simple restrictive pattern; this describes physiology and does not determine the underlying diagnosis.

templates.standard: Restriction is present with an increased residual-volume fraction and a preserved FEV1/FVC.
templates.expanded: The reduced TLC with disproportionately retained residual volume and a preserved ratio supports a complex restrictive pattern; reduced thoracic expansion and airway closure are possible contributors.

templates.standard: FEV1/FVC and TLC are below their LLNs, indicating mixed impairment.
templates.expanded: Both airflow obstruction and restriction are present, supported by a reduced FEV1/FVC and reduced TLC.

phrases.label: Obstruction and low FVC, TLC unavailable

templates.concise: Obstruction with reduced FVC; restriction is unconfirmed.
templates.standard: An obstructive pattern is present with a low FVC; TLC is required to assess for a concomitant restrictive component.
templates.expanded: The reduced FVC may reflect airway closure, gas trapping, or an additional restrictive process; spirometry alone cannot distinguish these.

phrases.label: Low FVC in obstruction, no restriction

templates.concise: Obstruction with low FVC and preserved TLC.
templates.standard: FVC is reduced in the setting of obstruction, without a reduced TLC.
templates.expanded: Restriction is not demonstrated by TLC; the low FVC may relate to airway closure or incomplete emptying rather than a restrictive component.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is present, with mild impairment in FEV1.
templates.expanded: FEV1/FVC is below the LLN; the reduction in FEV1 is mild using z-score grading.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is present, with moderate impairment in FEV1.
templates.expanded: FEV1/FVC is below the LLN; the reduction in FEV1 is moderate using z-score grading.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is present, with severe impairment in FEV1.
templates.expanded: FEV1/FVC is below the LLN; the reduction in FEV1 is severe using z-score grading.

phrases.label: Preserved ratio impaired spirometry phenotype

templates.standard: The configured definition of preserved ratio impaired spirometry is met.
templates.expanded: FEV1 is reduced with a preserved ratio according to the declared PRISm definition; this phenotype does not confirm restriction or identify a specific disease.

notes: Store the explicit ratio and FEV1 thresholds used; do not silently equate LLN-based findings with the common fixed-ratio/<80% epidemiologic definition.

phrases.label: Possible dysanaptic pattern

templates.concise: Low ratio with preserved flows and large FVC.
templates.standard: A reduced ratio with preserved FEV1 and a relatively large FVC may reflect a dysanaptic pattern.
templates.expanded: Airway-to-lung size mismatch is one possible explanation for the reduced ratio with preserved FEV1 and large FVC; symptoms, exposures, bronchodilator response, and longitudinal findings remain relevant.

notes: Do not dismiss abnormal ratios as a normal variant automatically.

templates.concise: Moderately severe obstructive ventilatory impairment by the selected legacy scheme.
templates.standard: Obstruction is graded moderately severe using the declared percent-predicted FEV1 scheme.
templates.expanded: The legacy percent-predicted FEV1 profile assigns moderately severe impairment; this label is not interchangeable with current z-score grading.

templates.concise: Very severe obstructive ventilatory impairment by the selected legacy scheme.
templates.standard: Obstruction is graded very severe using the declared percent-predicted FEV1 scheme.
templates.expanded: The legacy percent-predicted FEV1 profile assigns very severe impairment; this label is not interchangeable with current z-score grading.

templates.concise: {local_restriction_grade} restrictive impairment by the declared laboratory scheme.
templates.standard: Restriction is graded {local_restriction_grade} using {local_restriction_grading_basis}.
templates.expanded: Restriction is confirmed by reliable TLC and graded {local_restriction_grade} under the stated laboratory profile ({local_restriction_grading_basis}); the grading basis must be explicit.

templates.standard: Mid-expiratory flow is below its reference limit.
templates.expanded: Reduced FEF25–75 is a nonspecific finding and does not independently establish small airway disease.

templates.standard: FEF25–75 is reduced despite preserved conventional spirometric indices.
templates.expanded: An isolated low mid-expiratory flow should be interpreted cautiously because it is variable and depends on the measured FVC.

templates.standard: Mid-expiratory flow is within the expected reference range.
templates.expanded: A preserved FEF25–75 does not exclude small airway dysfunction and adds no independent disease exclusion.

templates.standard: FEF25–75 increases after bronchodilator administration.
templates.expanded: A change in FEF25–75 is descriptive; it should not be substituted for FEV1 or FVC criteria for a significant bronchodilator response.

templates.standard: Peak expiratory flow is below its reference range.
templates.expanded: Low peak flow may reflect airway limitation, a suboptimal start, or effort; interpret it with the loop and maneuver quality.

templates.standard: Peak expiratory flow is within reference limits.
templates.expanded: Peak expiratory flow is within reference limits; this does not exclude airflow limitation elsewhere in the maneuver.

templates.standard: Maximum voluntary ventilation is below its reference limit.
templates.expanded: Reduced measured MVV is nonspecific and may reflect airflow limitation, ventilatory mechanics, neuromuscular dysfunction, or effort.

templates.standard: Maximum voluntary ventilation is within reference limits.
templates.expanded: Measured MVV is within reference limits; the test remains effort dependent.

templates.concise: MVV is reduced out of proportion to FEV1.
templates.standard: Measured MVV is lower than expected from the spirometric findings.
templates.expanded: A disproportionate reduction in MVV may warrant review of effort, ventilatory mechanics, and respiratory muscle function; it is not diagnostic by itself.

templates.standard: MVV is calculated from FEV1 rather than directly measured.
templates.expanded: The reported MVV is an estimate using the configured multiplier and should not be interpreted as a direct endurance or muscle-strength measurement.

templates.standard: No reproducible loop abnormality is identified.
templates.expanded: The reviewed flow-volume loops show no reproducible abnormal contour; normal loops do not exclude intermittent upper-airway dysfunction.

templates.standard: The expiratory flow-volume limb shows concavity.
templates.expanded: Expiratory concavity supports airflow limitation when consistent with the measured indices, but is not specific for a particular airway disorder.

templates.concise: Loop volume is reduced with preserved contour.
templates.standard: The flow-volume loop is reduced in size with a relatively preserved shape.
templates.expanded: The small loop is compatible with a reduced vital capacity; restriction requires confirmation with TLC.

templates.standard: The inspiratory limb shows reproducible flattening.
templates.expanded: Reproducible inspiratory flattening raises concern for variable extrathoracic airflow limitation; correlate with symptoms and further airway evaluation when appropriate.

templates.standard: The expiratory limb shows reproducible flattening.
templates.expanded: Reproducible expiratory flattening may indicate variable intrathoracic central-airway limitation; loop review and clinical correlation are necessary.

templates.concise: Both loop limbs show reproducible flattening.
templates.standard: Reproducible flattening is present on both inspiratory and expiratory limbs.
templates.expanded: Flattening of both limbs raises concern for fixed central or upper-airway obstruction; this is a physiologic clue rather than an anatomic diagnosis.

templates.standard: Apparent loop flattening varies between efforts.
templates.expanded: Nonreproducible flattening may be technical or effort related and should not be used alone to diagnose central-airway obstruction.

templates.concise: An oscillatory loop contour is present.
templates.standard: The reviewed loop shows an oscillatory or sawtooth contour.
templates.expanded: An oscillatory loop contour is nonspecific; assess reproducibility, technique, and relevant upper-airway symptoms.

templates.standard: A reproducible biphasic expiratory contour is present.
templates.expanded: A biphasic expiratory contour may reflect heterogeneous emptying or central-airway mechanics; it does not identify a lesion on its own.

templates.standard: The volume-time curve shows prolonged expiratory emptying.
templates.expanded: Prolonged emptying is compatible with airflow limitation, provided the maneuver is acceptable; duration alone is not diagnostic.

templates.concise: An end-expiratory plateau was not achieved.
templates.standard: The volume-time curve lacks an end-expiratory plateau.
templates.expanded: Absence of a plateau requires review against the full end-of-test criteria; it is not, by itself, proof that every reported value is unusable.

templates.standard: No reproducible loop pattern suggesting central-airway obstruction is identified.
templates.expanded: The reviewed loops do not show a reproducible central-airway pattern; intermittent laryngeal obstruction cannot be excluded by a normal resting study.

templates.standard: FEV1 increases significantly after bronchodilator administration.
templates.expanded: The increase in FEV1 meets the selected bronchodilator-response criterion.

templates.standard: FVC increases significantly after bronchodilator administration.
templates.expanded: The increase in FVC meets the selected bronchodilator-response criterion; the mechanism is not established by this change alone.

templates.concise: Significant response in FEV1 and FVC.
templates.standard: Both FEV1 and FVC increase significantly after bronchodilator administration.
templates.expanded: Both spirometric measurements meet the selected response criterion.

templates.standard: Neither FEV1 nor FVC meets the selected criterion for a significant bronchodilator response.
templates.expanded: A significant spirometric response is not demonstrated on this occasion; this does not exclude asthma or symptomatic benefit from bronchodilator therapy.

templates.standard: No post-bronchodilator spirometry is available.
templates.expanded: Bronchodilator responsiveness cannot be assessed because pre- and post-bronchodilator measurements were not both obtained.

templates.standard: Technical limitations prevent reliable assessment of bronchodilator response.
templates.expanded: Pre- or post-bronchodilator maneuver quality, or missing required data, prevents a valid response classification.

templates.concise: FEV1 change {bd_fev1_pred_pct}% predicted; FVC change {bd_fvc_pred_pct}% predicted.
templates.standard: After bronchodilator, FEV1 changes by {bd_fev1_delta_mL} mL ({bd_fev1_pred_pct}% of predicted) and FVC by {bd_fvc_delta_mL} mL ({bd_fvc_pred_pct}% of predicted).
templates.expanded: Bronchodilator-response classification uses the changes relative to predicted FEV1 and FVC, rather than percent change from baseline.
templates.numeric: FEV1: {pre_fev1_L} to {post_fev1_L} L, Δ {bd_fev1_delta_mL} mL, {bd_fev1_pred_pct}% of predicted. FVC: {pre_fvc_L} to {post_fvc_L} L, Δ {bd_fvc_delta_mL} mL, {bd_fvc_pred_pct}% of predicted.

phrases.label: Legacy profile with numbers

templates.concise: Bronchodilator response assessed using the legacy baseline-change profile.
templates.standard: FEV1 changes by {bd_fev1_delta_mL} mL ({bd_fev1_baseline_pct}% from baseline); FVC changes by {bd_fvc_delta_mL} mL ({bd_fvc_baseline_pct}% from baseline).
templates.expanded: The laboratory-selected legacy profile is reported explicitly; it must not be silently combined with the current predicted-value response criterion.

notes: Exact endpoint operators must match the declared lab profile; historical statements and later summaries differ at the 200 mL boundary.

templates.standard: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC is no longer below the LLN.
templates.expanded: The previously reduced ratio normalizes after bronchodilator administration; ratio normalization and a significant volume response should be reported separately.

templates.standard: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC remains below the LLN.
templates.expanded: An obstructive ventilatory impairment remains after bronchodilator administration; this can coexist with a significant FEV1 or FVC response.

templates.concise: Normal baseline spirometry with a significant bronchodilator response.
templates.standard: A significant bronchodilator response is present despite baseline spirometry within reference limits.
templates.expanded: The measured response is compatible with variable airway physiology, but does not by itself establish a clinical diagnosis of asthma.

templates.standard: The bronchodilator response is predominantly a change in FVC.
templates.expanded: A predominant FVC response may reflect reduced airway closure or improved emptying; matched maneuver quality is essential before attributing the change to physiology.

templates.concise: There is a subthreshold increase after bronchodilator.
templates.standard: Measured spirometric improvement does not meet the selected significance criterion.
templates.expanded: FEV1 and/or FVC increase after bronchodilator, but the changes remain below the selected technical threshold; clinical response cannot be determined from this result alone.

phrases.label: Post-bronchodilator decrease

templates.standard: FEV1 and/or FVC decrease on post-bronchodilator testing.
templates.expanded: The lower post-bronchodilator values warrant review of effort, technique, fatigue, and timing before a physiologic explanation is assigned.

notes: Do not automatically diagnose paradoxical bronchospasm.

templates.concise: Recent medication use may affect the measured response.
templates.standard: Bronchodilator medication was not withheld according to the testing protocol.
templates.expanded: Recent bronchodilator use may blunt the measured incremental response; record the medication and timing when known.

templates.concise: Current and legacy response classifications differ.
templates.standard: The response meets {bd_met_profile} criteria but not {bd_unmet_profile} criteria.
templates.expanded: Different response definitions yield different classifications; the selected laboratory standard and the raw changes should be stated.

templates.standard: TLC is within reference limits relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: TLC is within reference limits. Restriction is defined by a reliable TLC below the LLN; an isolated high TLC does not determine its cause.

templates.standard: TLC is reduced relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: TLC is reduced. Restriction is defined by a reliable TLC below the LLN; an isolated high TLC does not determine its cause.

templates.standard: TLC is increased relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: TLC is increased. Restriction is defined by a reliable TLC below the LLN; an isolated high TLC does not determine its cause.

templates.standard: RV is within reference limits relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: RV is within reference limits. Interpret residual volume alongside TLC and RV/TLC rather than assigning a mechanism from RV alone.

templates.standard: RV is reduced relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: RV is reduced. Interpret residual volume alongside TLC and RV/TLC rather than assigning a mechanism from RV alone.

templates.standard: RV is increased relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: RV is increased. Interpret residual volume alongside TLC and RV/TLC rather than assigning a mechanism from RV alone.

templates.standard: FRC is within reference limits relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: FRC is within reference limits. Interpret the resting lung volume alongside TLC, FRC/TLC, and the measured volume distribution.

templates.standard: FRC is reduced relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: FRC is reduced. Interpret the resting lung volume alongside TLC, FRC/TLC, and the measured volume distribution.

templates.standard: FRC is increased relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: FRC is increased. Interpret the resting lung volume alongside TLC, FRC/TLC, and the measured volume distribution.

templates.standard: ERV is within reference limits relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: ERV is within reference limits. A reduced ERV is nonspecific and may accompany body habitus, posture, or altered respiratory mechanics.

templates.standard: ERV is reduced relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: ERV is reduced. A reduced ERV is nonspecific and may accompany body habitus, posture, or altered respiratory mechanics.

templates.standard: ERV is increased relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: ERV is increased. A reduced ERV is nonspecific and may accompany body habitus, posture, or altered respiratory mechanics.

templates.standard: IC is within reference limits relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: IC is within reference limits. A reduced IC may relate to an elevated resting lung volume, a reduced TLC, or limited inspiration.

templates.standard: IC is reduced relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: IC is reduced. A reduced IC may relate to an elevated resting lung volume, a reduced TLC, or limited inspiration.

templates.standard: IC is increased relative to the selected reference equation.
templates.expanded: IC is increased. A reduced IC may relate to an elevated resting lung volume, a reduced TLC, or limited inspiration.

templates.standard: RV/TLC is within reference limits.
templates.expanded: RV/TLC is within reference limits; interpret with the absolute volumes.

templates.standard: RV/TLC is above the upper limit of normal.
templates.expanded: RV/TLC is elevated; interpretation depends on absolute volumes, TLC, and maneuver quality.

templates.standard: FRC/TLC is within reference limits.
templates.expanded: FRC/TLC is within reference limits; interpret with the absolute volumes.

templates.standard: FRC/TLC is above the upper limit of normal.
templates.expanded: FRC/TLC is elevated; interpretation depends on absolute volumes, TLC, and maneuver quality.

templates.concise: Lung volumes are within reference limits.
templates.standard: The measured lung volumes and volume fractions are within reference limits.
templates.expanded: The available reliable lung-volume measurements show no restrictive or hyperinflation pattern.

templates.concise: Lung volumes show an air-trapping pattern.
templates.standard: RV/TLC is increased with a non-reduced TLC, supporting air trapping.
templates.expanded: An increased residual-volume fraction with a reliable, non-reduced TLC supports air trapping; respiratory muscle weakness and maneuver quality can affect this pattern.

templates.standard: The resting and residual-volume fractions are elevated, supporting hyperinflation.
templates.expanded: Elevated FRC/TLC and RV/TLC with a non-reduced TLC support hyperinflation; TLC may remain within reference limits.

templates.standard: TLC is increased with elevated resting or residual-volume fractions.
templates.expanded: An increased TLC accompanied by elevated volume fractions supports hyperinflation rather than simply large lungs.

templates.concise: Large lung volumes with preserved volume fractions.
templates.standard: TLC is above the ULN with preserved RV/TLC and FRC/TLC.
templates.expanded: The high TLC with preserved volume fractions may represent constitutionally large lungs; this is not sufficient to identify disease-related hyperinflation.

templates.concise: RV/TLC is increased in the setting of reduced TLC.
templates.standard: An increased residual-volume fraction accompanies a reduced TLC.
templates.expanded: The elevated RV/TLC may partly reflect the lower TLC; it should not automatically be labeled air trapping without review of absolute RV and the overall pattern.

templates.concise: RV is increased with a preserved RV/TLC.
templates.standard: Residual volume is high in proportion to the total lung volume.
templates.expanded: An increased absolute RV with a preserved RV/TLC does not independently establish air trapping.

templates.standard: TLC and fractional lung volumes are unavailable.
templates.expanded: Restriction, mixed impairment, and volume-distribution abnormalities cannot be assessed directly without reliable lung-volume measurements.

templates.standard: ERV is reduced while TLC remains within reference limits.
templates.expanded: This volume distribution may reflect body habitus or other extrapulmonary mechanics; it is not specific for obesity.

templates.standard: Plethysmographic TLC differs from gas-dilution TLC.
templates.expanded: A method-dependent difference may reflect noncommunicating gas, ventilation heterogeneity, or technical factors; both methods and quality should be stated.
templates.numeric: TLC is {tlc_pleth_L} L by plethysmography and {tlc_dilution_L} L by {dilution_method}.

templates.concise: Gas dilution may underestimate total lung volume.
templates.standard: Ventilation heterogeneity may limit the gas-dilution lung-volume measurement.
templates.expanded: Poorly communicating lung regions may be incompletely sampled by gas dilution; apparent restriction requires careful method and quality review.

templates.standard: Diffusing capacity is within the expected reference range.
templates.expanded: DLCO is within reference limits on the reported adjustment basis; a normal value does not exclude early lung or pulmonary vascular disease.

templates.standard: Diffusing capacity is below the LLN.
templates.expanded: The reduced DLCO indicates impaired measured carbon-monoxide transfer; its mechanism requires integration with volumes, VA, KCO, hemoglobin, and clinical findings.

templates.standard: Diffusing capacity is above the ULN.
templates.expanded: DLCO exceeds the reference range; interpret with hemoglobin, test quality, and the clinical setting.

templates.standard: No diffusing-capacity measurement is available.
templates.expanded: Gas-transfer function cannot be assessed from this study because DLCO was not obtained.

templates.standard: No reliable diffusing-capacity measurement was obtained.
templates.expanded: DLCO maneuver quality does not support a reliable assessment of gas-transfer function.

templates.standard: Diffusing capacity is reduced to a mild degree.
templates.expanded: The reduction in DLCO represents mild gas-transfer impairment by the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: DLCO is {dlco_pct_pred}% predicted (z-score {dlco_z}), a mild reduction.

templates.standard: Diffusing capacity is reduced to a moderate degree.
templates.expanded: The reduction in DLCO represents moderate gas-transfer impairment by the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: DLCO is {dlco_pct_pred}% predicted (z-score {dlco_z}), a moderate reduction.

templates.standard: Diffusing capacity is reduced to a severe degree.
templates.expanded: The reduction in DLCO represents severe gas-transfer impairment by the selected z-score grading scheme.
templates.numeric: DLCO is {dlco_pct_pred}% predicted (z-score {dlco_z}), a severe reduction.

templates.standard: DLCO interpretation incorporates measured hemoglobin.
templates.expanded: The reported DLCO comparison is hemoglobin adjusted using the laboratory method; record the hemoglobin value and its date.

templates.concise: DLCO is not adjusted for hemoglobin.
templates.standard: The reported DLCO is not hemoglobin adjusted.
templates.expanded: Anemia or an elevated hemoglobin may affect the unadjusted DLCO; this limitation should be stated rather than assuming a normal hemoglobin.

templates.standard: The hemoglobin-adjustment basis is not established.
templates.expanded: The available metadata do not establish whether DLCO was adjusted for hemoglobin; avoid describing the value as corrected or uncorrected until this is clarified.

templates.concise: Anemia may contribute to the reduced DLCO.
templates.standard: The low hemoglobin may partly explain a reduced unadjusted DLCO.
templates.expanded: Because the reported DLCO is unadjusted and anemia is documented, the gas-transfer deficit may partly reflect reduced hemoglobin rather than only pulmonary pathology.

phrases.label: Reference comparison normal after Hb adjustment

templates.concise: DLCO is within reference limits after hemoglobin adjustment.
templates.standard: The hemoglobin-adjusted DLCO is within reference limits despite a low unadjusted comparison.
templates.expanded: Hemoglobin adjustment changes the DLCO reference classification; retain the adjustment method and measured hemoglobin in the report.

templates.concise: DLCO remains reduced after hemoglobin adjustment.
templates.standard: Hemoglobin-adjusted diffusing capacity remains below the LLN.
templates.expanded: The gas-transfer impairment persists on the hemoglobin-adjusted comparison and is not explained solely by the documented hemoglobin level.

templates.standard: Recent smoking or elevated carboxyhemoglobin may influence DLCO.
templates.expanded: The documented smoking or carboxyhemoglobin context may affect the DLCO measurement; state any laboratory correction that was actually applied.

templates.standard: Supplemental oxygen exposure may influence the DLCO measurement.
templates.expanded: The oxygen conditions during testing should be documented; do not invent a room-air measurement or oxygen correction.

templates.standard: DLCO is reduced with preserved spirometry and lung volumes.
templates.expanded: An isolated gas-transfer deficit is present; PFTs alone do not distinguish its possible causes.

templates.concise: Consider pulmonary vascular or early parenchymal causes.
templates.standard: A low DLCO with preserved volumes may be seen with pulmonary vascular disease, emphysema, early parenchymal disease, or anemia.
templates.expanded: Interpret the isolated DLCO deficit with imaging, hemoglobin, symptoms, and cardiac or vascular assessment; none of these diagnoses is established by the PFT alone.

templates.standard: An increased DLCO may occur with increased pulmonary blood volume, elevated hemoglobin, asthma, or alveolar hemorrhage.
templates.expanded: The high DLCO should be interpreted in the relevant clinical setting and after reviewing technique; it is not independently diagnostic of asthma or alveolar hemorrhage.

templates.concise: {legacy_dlco_grade} reduction in DLCO by the selected legacy scheme.
templates.standard: The reduction in DLCO is graded {legacy_dlco_grade} using {legacy_dlco_profile}.
templates.expanded: The stated DLCO grade follows the declared percent-predicted legacy profile; it should not be combined with an unlabeled z-score classification.

templates.standard: VA is within reference limits relative to its reference range.
templates.expanded: VA is within reference limits. VA represents the lung volume sampled by the single-breath maneuver, not an independent measurement of TLC.

templates.standard: VA is reduced relative to its reference range.
templates.expanded: VA is reduced. VA represents the lung volume sampled by the single-breath maneuver, not an independent measurement of TLC.

templates.standard: VA is increased relative to its reference range.
templates.expanded: VA is increased. VA represents the lung volume sampled by the single-breath maneuver, not an independent measurement of TLC.

templates.standard: KCO is within reference limits relative to its reference range.
templates.expanded: KCO is within reference limits. Interpret KCO alongside VA and DLCO rather than as a volume correction that removes a gas-transfer deficit.

templates.standard: KCO is reduced relative to its reference range.
templates.expanded: KCO is reduced. Interpret KCO alongside VA and DLCO rather than as a volume correction that removes a gas-transfer deficit.

templates.standard: KCO is increased relative to its reference range.
templates.expanded: KCO is increased. Interpret KCO alongside VA and DLCO rather than as a volume correction that removes a gas-transfer deficit.

phrases.label: Low DLCO, preserved VA, low KCO

templates.concise: Low DLCO with preserved VA and reduced KCO.
templates.standard: The gas-transfer deficit is accompanied by a reduced transfer coefficient and preserved sampled alveolar volume.
templates.expanded: The reduced DLCO with preserved VA and low KCO supports reduced transfer efficiency; the PFT does not identify its cause.

phrases.label: Low DLCO, low VA and low KCO

templates.concise: DLCO, VA, and KCO are reduced.
templates.standard: The low DLCO reflects both reduced sampled alveolar volume and a low transfer coefficient.
templates.expanded: Both VA and KCO are reduced, indicating that the low DLCO is not explained only by a smaller sampled volume.

phrases.label: Low DLCO, low VA, preserved KCO

templates.concise: Low DLCO and VA with preserved KCO.
templates.standard: DLCO and VA are reduced, while KCO remains within reference limits.
templates.expanded: A preserved KCO does not negate the reduced DLCO; interpret the smaller sampled volume in light of inspiration, TLC, and ventilation distribution.

phrases.label: Low DLCO, low VA, high KCO

templates.concise: Low DLCO and VA with increased KCO.
templates.standard: DLCO and VA are reduced, while KCO is increased.
templates.expanded: An increased KCO with a small VA may accompany incomplete expansion or reduced accessible lung volume; it does not establish normal overall gas transfer.

templates.concise: VA is low relative to measured TLC.
templates.standard: The single-breath sampled volume is reduced relative to the independently measured TLC.
templates.expanded: A reduced VA/TLC may indicate ventilation maldistribution or incomplete sampling; assess inspired volume and method quality before assigning a mechanism.

templates.concise: VA is proportionate to measured TLC.
templates.standard: The sampled alveolar volume is proportionate to the independently measured TLC.
templates.expanded: VA/TLC is preserved using the laboratory reference or reviewed comparison; this does not by itself exclude parenchymal disease.

templates.concise: Reduced VA may reflect incomplete lung expansion.
templates.standard: The low sampled volume may relate to incomplete expansion or extrapulmonary mechanics.
templates.expanded: Reduced VA with preserved or increased KCO may favor incomplete expansion in the appropriate clinical setting; quality, TLC, and imaging are required for interpretation.

templates.standard: MIP magnitude is within its reference range.
templates.expanded: MIP magnitude is within reference limits on this effort-dependent test.
templates.numeric: MIP is {mip_display_cmH2O} cm H2O ({mip_pct_pred}% predicted; magnitude LLN {mip_magnitude_lln_cmH2O} cm H2O).

templates.standard: MIP magnitude is below the LLN.
templates.expanded: MIP is low; this may reflect muscle weakness, submaximal effort, or technical limitations.
templates.numeric: MIP is {mip_display_cmH2O} cm H2O ({mip_pct_pred}% predicted; magnitude LLN {mip_magnitude_lln_cmH2O} cm H2O).

templates.standard: MEP magnitude is within its reference range.
templates.expanded: MEP magnitude is within reference limits on this effort-dependent test.
templates.numeric: MEP is {mep_display_cmH2O} cm H2O ({mep_pct_pred}% predicted; magnitude LLN {mep_magnitude_lln_cmH2O} cm H2O).

templates.standard: MEP magnitude is below the LLN.
templates.expanded: MEP is low; this may reflect muscle weakness, submaximal effort, or technical limitations.
templates.numeric: MEP is {mep_display_cmH2O} cm H2O ({mep_pct_pred}% predicted; magnitude LLN {mep_magnitude_lln_cmH2O} cm H2O).

templates.standard: SNIP magnitude is within its reference range.
templates.expanded: SNIP magnitude is within reference limits on this effort-dependent test.
templates.numeric: SNIP is {snip_display_cmH2O} cm H2O ({snip_pct_pred}% predicted; magnitude LLN {snip_magnitude_lln_cmH2O} cm H2O).

templates.standard: SNIP magnitude is below the LLN.
templates.expanded: SNIP is low; this may reflect muscle weakness, submaximal effort, or technical limitations.
templates.numeric: SNIP is {snip_display_cmH2O} cm H2O ({snip_pct_pred}% predicted; magnitude LLN {snip_magnitude_lln_cmH2O} cm H2O).

templates.standard: Inspiratory and expiratory pressure magnitudes are below their reference limits.
templates.expanded: Low MIP and MEP raise concern for generalized respiratory muscle weakness when supported by reliable effort and the clinical setting.

templates.concise: MIP is reduced with preserved MEP.
templates.standard: Inspiratory pressure is reduced while expiratory pressure remains within reference limits.
templates.expanded: This pattern raises concern for inspiratory muscle dysfunction, but low volitional MIP is not specific for diaphragmatic weakness.

templates.concise: MEP is reduced with preserved MIP.
templates.standard: Expiratory pressure is reduced while inspiratory pressure remains within reference limits.
templates.expanded: This pattern may reflect expiratory muscle dysfunction or technique; it does not by itself establish ineffective cough.

templates.standard: Inspiratory and expiratory pressure magnitudes are within reference limits.
templates.expanded: These volitional pressure measurements do not demonstrate reduced respiratory muscle strength; intermittent dysfunction or other limitations may require additional evaluation.

templates.standard: Vital capacity decreases by {supine_vc_drop_pct}% from upright to supine.
templates.expanded: The postural decrease in vital capacity is reported as a relative change from the upright measurement; interpretation depends on reproducibility and the clinical setting.
templates.numeric: Upright VC {upright_vc_L} L; supine VC {supine_vc_L} L; decrease {supine_vc_drop_pct}%.

phrases.label: Postural decrease concerning for diaphragm dysfunction

templates.concise: Postural VC decline raises concern for diaphragmatic dysfunction.
templates.standard: The reproducible fall in VC when supine is greater than expected for the testing method.
templates.expanded: An excessive postural fall in vital capacity supports possible diaphragmatic dysfunction in the appropriate clinical setting; it is not diagnostic on its own.

notes: The 2019 ERS statement discusses a 15% decrease as a useful screening clue; thresholds vary by question, method, and baseline mechanics. Do not turn it into a universal diagnosis rule.

templates.concise: No excessive postural fall in VC.
templates.standard: Upright-to-supine VC change is not excessive by the selected laboratory criterion.
templates.expanded: No excessive postural decline is identified using the selected criterion; this does not exclude all respiratory muscle dysfunction.

templates.standard: A reliable upright-to-supine VC comparison could not be obtained.
templates.expanded: Postural vital-capacity testing was incomplete or technically limited; diaphragmatic function cannot be inferred from this comparison.

templates.standard: Restriction is accompanied by reduced MIP and/or MEP.
templates.expanded: Respiratory muscle dysfunction may contribute to the restrictive physiology if the pressure measurements are reliable and the clinical setting supports this interpretation.

templates.standard: Peak cough flow measures {pcf_L_min} L/min under {pcf_condition} conditions.
templates.expanded: The measured cough flow is {pcf_L_min} L/min; document whether the effort was spontaneous, coached, assisted, or obtained through an artificial airway.

phrases.label: Reduced cough flow by configured context

templates.concise: Cough flow is reduced by the selected clinical criterion.
templates.standard: Peak cough flow is below the threshold selected for this clinical context.
templates.expanded: Reduced cough flow may indicate limited airway-clearance reserve; thresholds and interventions are disease- and method-dependent.

notes: Do not apply 160 or 270 L/min as universal adult reference limits or automatically infer need for a device.

templates.concise: Bulbar or mouth-seal limitations affect pressure testing.
templates.standard: Orofacial or bulbar dysfunction limits mouth-pressure reliability.
templates.expanded: An inadequate seal or impaired coordination can produce low MIP/MEP without establishing the degree of respiratory muscle weakness; consider an alternative method when clinically appropriate.

templates.standard: A protocol-defined fall in FEV1 is reached during methacholine challenge.
templates.expanded: The challenge demonstrates airway hyperresponsiveness; the result supports clinical assessment but does not independently establish asthma.

templates.concise: Methacholine challenge is negative at the tested limit.
templates.standard: No protocol-defined FEV1 response is reached at the maximum completed dose.
templates.expanded: The completed challenge does not demonstrate airway hyperresponsiveness at the tested limit; medication use and symptom timing affect its diagnostic implications.

templates.standard: Testing stopped before completion of the planned challenge protocol.
templates.expanded: The challenge cannot be labeled a fully negative study because the planned maximum dose was not completed.

templates.standard: Technical limitations prevent reliable challenge interpretation.
templates.expanded: The available dose-response measurements do not support a reliable determination of airway responsiveness.

templates.standard: FEV1 changes substantially after diluent or during baseline assessment.
templates.expanded: A diluent response or unstable baseline limits the reliability of the subsequent methacholine dose-response comparison.

templates.standard: The delivered dose provoking a 20% fall in FEV1 is {pd20_value} {pd20_unit}.
templates.expanded: The methacholine dose-response result is reported as protocol-specific PD20; concentration and delivered-dose values are not interchangeable.

templates.standard: The concentration provoking a 20% fall in FEV1 is {pc20_mg_mL} mg/mL using {methacholine_protocol}.
templates.expanded: PC20 is reported for the documented concentration-based protocol; the method is needed to interpret or compare the value.

templates.standard: A 20% fall in FEV1 is not reached through {max_pd_value} {max_pd_unit}.
templates.expanded: The completed dose sequence establishes a lower bound on PD20; report greater than the maximum delivered dose rather than inventing an exact PD20.

templates.standard: A 20% fall in FEV1 is not reached through {max_pc20_mg_mL} mg/mL.
templates.expanded: The completed concentration sequence establishes a lower bound on PC20 for this protocol; it does not provide an exact concentration response.

phrases.label: Borderline AHR

templates.standard: The methacholine response falls in the borderline AHR range for the documented protocol.
templates.expanded: The protocol-specific result indicates borderline airway hyperresponsiveness; this grading is not a measure of asthma severity.

notes: Use the laboratory-supplied or explicitly configured protocol-specific category; shared printed endpoints require a documented implementation convention.

phrases.label: Mild AHR

templates.standard: The methacholine response falls in the mild AHR range for the documented protocol.
templates.expanded: The protocol-specific result indicates mild airway hyperresponsiveness; this grading is not a measure of asthma severity.

notes: Use the laboratory-supplied or explicitly configured protocol-specific category; shared printed endpoints require a documented implementation convention.

phrases.label: Moderate AHR

templates.standard: The methacholine response falls in the moderate AHR range for the documented protocol.
templates.expanded: The protocol-specific result indicates moderate airway hyperresponsiveness; this grading is not a measure of asthma severity.

notes: Use the laboratory-supplied or explicitly configured protocol-specific category; shared printed endpoints require a documented implementation convention.

phrases.label: Marked AHR

templates.standard: The methacholine response falls in the marked AHR range for the documented protocol.
templates.expanded: The protocol-specific result indicates marked airway hyperresponsiveness; this grading is not a measure of asthma severity.

notes: Use the laboratory-supplied or explicitly configured protocol-specific category; shared printed endpoints require a documented implementation convention.

templates.concise: A completed negative test lowers the probability of current asthma.
templates.standard: A negative challenge during an appropriate symptomatic period makes current asthma less likely.
templates.expanded: The implication of a negative challenge depends on medication withholding, adequate dose delivery, and symptoms at the time of testing; it does not exclude every asthma phenotype.

templates.concise: Medication use may blunt challenge responsiveness.
templates.standard: Relevant medication was not withheld according to the challenge protocol.
templates.expanded: Recent bronchodilator or other relevant medication use may reduce challenge responsiveness; record the drug and timing and avoid an unqualified negative interpretation.

templates.standard: FEV1 returns to {recovery_pct_baseline}% of the challenge baseline after bronchodilator.
templates.expanded: Post-challenge recovery is documented by repeat FEV1, rather than inferred from symptom improvement alone.

templates.standard: Exercise challenge meets the selected FEV1-response criterion.
templates.expanded: A protocol-defined physiologic response is present; interpret with symptoms, medication use, and test conditions.

templates.concise: Exercise challenge is negative at the completed protocol limit.
templates.standard: Exercise challenge does not meet the selected FEV1-response criterion.
templates.expanded: No qualifying response was measured under the completed test conditions; an inadequate stimulus or medication effect must be considered when relevant.

templates.standard: Adequate completion of the exercise protocol was not achieved.
templates.expanded: The result cannot establish absence of responsiveness because the required stimulus or measurement sequence was not completed.

templates.concise: Eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea challenge is positive.
templates.standard: Eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea challenge meets the selected FEV1-response criterion.
templates.expanded: A protocol-defined physiologic response is present; interpret with symptoms, medication use, and test conditions.

templates.concise: Eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea challenge is negative at the completed protocol limit.
templates.standard: Eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea challenge does not meet the selected FEV1-response criterion.
templates.expanded: No qualifying response was measured under the completed test conditions; an inadequate stimulus or medication effect must be considered when relevant.

templates.concise: Eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea challenge is incomplete.
templates.standard: Adequate completion of the evh protocol was not achieved.
templates.expanded: The result cannot establish absence of responsiveness because the required stimulus or measurement sequence was not completed.

templates.standard: Mannitol challenge meets the selected FEV1-response criterion.
templates.expanded: A protocol-defined physiologic response is present; interpret with symptoms, medication use, and test conditions.

templates.concise: Mannitol challenge is negative at the completed protocol limit.
templates.standard: Mannitol challenge does not meet the selected FEV1-response criterion.
templates.expanded: No qualifying response was measured under the completed test conditions; an inadequate stimulus or medication effect must be considered when relevant.

templates.standard: Adequate completion of the mannitol protocol was not achieved.
templates.expanded: The result cannot establish absence of responsiveness because the required stimulus or measurement sequence was not completed.

templates.standard: FEV1 falls by a maximum of {exercise_fev1_fall_pct}% from baseline at {exercise_nadir_minutes} minutes after exercise.
templates.expanded: The response is quantified from valid serial FEV1 measurements and the documented baseline; record the adequacy of the exercise stimulus.

templates.standard: The cumulative mannitol dose provoking a 15% fall in FEV1 is {mannitol_pd15_mg} mg.
templates.expanded: The mannitol response is quantified using the protocol-specific cumulative dose; a methacholine PD20 is a different measure.

templates.standard: FeNO is below the adult low-level threshold.
templates.expanded: Low FeNO makes substantial eosinophilic airway inflammation less likely in the appropriate setting; smoking and anti-inflammatory treatment may affect the value.

templates.concise: FeNO is in the intermediate range.
templates.standard: FeNO is intermediate by the adult ATS categories.
templates.expanded: An intermediate FeNO should be interpreted with symptoms, atopy, treatment, and other evidence of airway inflammation.

templates.standard: FeNO is high by the adult ATS categories.
templates.expanded: A high FeNO supports eosinophilic airway inflammation and potential corticosteroid responsiveness in the appropriate clinical setting; it does not independently diagnose asthma.

templates.concise: FeNO is low while on inhaled corticosteroid therapy.
templates.standard: The FeNO value was obtained during inhaled corticosteroid treatment.
templates.expanded: A low FeNO on inhaled corticosteroids may reflect treatment suppression and should not be used alone to exclude a history of eosinophilic airway disease.

templates.concise: FeNO remains high during inhaled corticosteroid therapy.
templates.standard: FeNO is elevated despite reported inhaled corticosteroid use.
templates.expanded: The high FeNO warrants review of treatment use, inhaler technique, allergen exposure, and the clinical setting; it does not prove nonadherence.

templates.standard: Technical limitations affect the FeNO measurement.
templates.expanded: FeNO quality, exhalation flow, and measurement conditions require review before a category or treatment implication is assigned.

templates.standard: Measured airway resistance is above its reference limit.
templates.expanded: The increased Raw is compatible with altered airway mechanics but depends on lung volume and technique.

templates.concise: Airway resistance is within reference limits.
templates.standard: Raw is within the laboratory reference range.
templates.expanded: Raw is preserved using the selected method; this does not exclude airway disease.

templates.standard: sGaw is below its reference limit.
templates.expanded: A reduced sGaw supports impaired conductance in the tested conditions but is not diagnostic of a particular airway disorder.

templates.standard: sGaw is within the laboratory reference range.
templates.expanded: Specific conductance is within reference limits using the selected method and lung-volume basis.

templates.standard: Raw decreases and/or sGaw increases after bronchodilator.
templates.expanded: A change in resistance or conductance is described using the laboratory criterion and must not be substituted for spirometric response criteria.

templates.standard: The reported resistance and reactance indices are within their reference limits.
templates.expanded: The valid oscillometry indices are within the configured device- and reference-specific ranges.

templates.standard: Resistance at 5 Hz is above its reference limit.
templates.expanded: Increased R5 reflects altered respiratory-system resistance; it is not specific for small airway disease.

templates.standard: The difference between low- and higher-frequency resistance is increased.
templates.expanded: Increased R5–R20 is compatible with heterogeneous airway mechanics in the appropriate setting; it is not a direct measurement of peripheral-airway resistance.

templates.concise: Low-frequency reactance is more negative than expected.
templates.standard: Reactance at 5 Hz is below its lower reference limit.
templates.expanded: A more negative X5 supports abnormal respiratory mechanics; the cause requires integration with volumes and other findings.

templates.standard: AX is above its reference limit.
templates.expanded: An increased reactance area indicates abnormal respiratory-system reactance using the selected device and reference.

templates.standard: The resonant frequency is above the selected reference limit.
templates.expanded: An increased resonant frequency is a nonspecific marker of altered respiratory mechanics.

templates.standard: The change in oscillometry meets the selected response criterion.
templates.expanded: An oscillometric response is present using the declared device- and index-specific criterion; this is separate from spirometric bronchodilator responsiveness.

templates.standard: Artifacts or inconsistent acquisitions limit oscillometry interpretation.
templates.expanded: Oscillometry quality is limited by the documented acquisition or artifact issue; unreliable values should not drive disease classification.

phrases.label: Increased LCI

templates.standard: LCI is above the method-specific reference limit.
templates.expanded: An increased LCI supports ventilation inhomogeneity using the validated method and reference; it does not identify a specific disease.

notes: Basic wording only. Implementation requires the lab-selected washout standard and device validation beyond this package.

phrases.label: Normal LCI

templates.concise: Lung clearance index is within reference limits.
templates.standard: LCI is within the method-specific reference range.
templates.expanded: The washout result does not demonstrate increased LCI using the selected method and reference.

notes: Basic wording only. Implementation requires the lab-selected washout standard and device validation beyond this package.

phrases.label: Washout quality limitation

templates.standard: Leak, breathing irregularity, or incomplete washout affects the measurement.
templates.expanded: The observed washout quality limitation prevents an unqualified ventilation-distribution interpretation.

notes: Basic wording only. Implementation requires the lab-selected washout standard and device validation beyond this package.

templates.standard: The patient walks {walk_distance_m} m in six minutes under the documented test conditions.
templates.expanded: Six-minute walk distance is {walk_distance_m} m; record oxygen support, walking aid, interruptions, and the reason for any limitation.

templates.concise: Walk distance is below the selected reference range.
templates.standard: Six-minute walk distance is reduced relative to the validated reference.
templates.expanded: A reduced distance reflects functional limitation but is not specific for a pulmonary mechanism.

templates.concise: No qualifying exertional desaturation is demonstrated.
templates.standard: Saturation does not cross the selected desaturation threshold during the completed test.
templates.expanded: No qualifying desaturation is measured with an adequate signal under the recorded oxygen conditions; this does not establish room-air oxygenation if supplemental oxygen was used.

templates.standard: SpO2 falls from {walk_baseline_spo2}% to a nadir of {walk_nadir_spo2}% during walking.
templates.expanded: A reproducible decline in saturation is observed with an adequate signal; state the oxygen support rather than inferring its cause.

templates.standard: Oxygen support during the walk is {walk_oxygen_description}.
templates.expanded: The distance and oxygenation findings apply to the recorded device and setting; continuous-flow and pulse-dose settings are not interchangeable.

templates.concise: The recorded oxygen setting maintains the selected saturation target.
templates.standard: During the observed titration, {titration_oxygen_description} maintains SpO2 at or above {target_spo2}%.
templates.expanded: The reported oxygen setting achieves the selected target during this test; a prescription requires clinical review of device, activity, and context.

templates.standard: The walk stops after {walk_duration_min} minutes because of {walk_limiting_symptom}.
templates.expanded: The test was not completed; report achieved time and distance without presenting them as a completed six-minute result.

templates.standard: Motion or poor signal quality limits the saturation measurement.
templates.expanded: The saturation trace is not sufficiently reliable for an unqualified desaturation interpretation.

templates.concise: No prior comparable PFT is available.
templates.standard: No suitable prior study is available for comparison.
templates.expanded: A longitudinal change cannot be assessed because a comparable prior measurement is unavailable.

templates.standard: There is no meaningful interval change in the reviewed comparable measurements.
templates.expanded: The observed differences are judged not clinically meaningful after reviewing test quality, methods, and the clinical context.

templates.concise: FEV1 is lower than on the prior study.
templates.standard: FEV1 decreases by {serial_fev1_delta_mL_abs} mL from {prior_date} to {current_date}.
templates.expanded: FEV1 is lower on the comparable study; the magnitude, quality, and clinical context determine the importance of this change.

templates.concise: FEV1 is higher than on the prior study.
templates.standard: FEV1 increases by {serial_fev1_delta_mL_abs} mL from {prior_date} to {current_date}.
templates.expanded: FEV1 is higher on the comparable study; this descriptive change does not identify the cause.

templates.concise: FVC is lower than on the prior study.
templates.standard: FVC decreases from {prior_fvc_L} to {current_fvc_L} L.
templates.expanded: The change in FVC is reported numerically; reduced effort, airway closure, and a restrictive process remain possible explanations depending on the full study.

templates.concise: FVC is higher than on the prior study.
templates.standard: FVC increases from {prior_fvc_L} to {current_fvc_L} L.
templates.expanded: FVC is higher on the comparable measurement; interpretation requires attention to testing state and quality.

templates.concise: TLC is lower than on the prior study.
templates.standard: TLC decreases from {prior_tlc_L} to {current_tlc_L} L.
templates.expanded: The lung-volume change should be evaluated using matched methods, reliable maneuvers, and the accompanying spirometric findings.

templates.concise: DLCO is lower than on the prior study.
templates.standard: DLCO decreases from {prior_dlco_value} to {current_dlco_value} {dlco_units}.
templates.expanded: The gas-transfer change requires matched hemoglobin-adjustment and testing conditions before attributing it to pulmonary progression.

templates.concise: DLCO is higher than on the prior study.
templates.standard: DLCO increases from {prior_dlco_value} to {current_dlco_value} {dlco_units}.
templates.expanded: The higher gas-transfer measurement should be interpreted with hemoglobin, test quality, and the clinical context.

templates.standard: {serial_metric_label} changes from {prior_pct_pred}% to {current_pct_pred}% predicted, a difference of {serial_signed_pp_change} percentage points.
templates.expanded: The stated change is an absolute difference in percent-predicted values, not a relative percent change from baseline.

templates.standard: The relative change in {serial_metric_label} from the prior measured value is {serial_relative_pct}%.
templates.expanded: Relative change uses the prior measured value as the denominator and should not be confused with percentage-point change in percent predicted.

templates.standard: Percent-predicted values and z-scores use different reference equations.
templates.expanded: Part of the reported reference-normalized change may reflect the equation change; compare measured values and consider recomputation using a common valid reference.

templates.standard: A method difference limits direct longitudinal comparison.
templates.expanded: Differences in equipment, lung-volume method, or testing protocol may contribute to the apparent change.

templates.standard: Differences in maneuver quality reduce confidence in the interval change.
templates.expanded: The measured change may be influenced by unequal test quality; avoid an unqualified progression or improvement statement.

templates.standard: The two DLCO studies use different hemoglobin-adjustment bases.
templates.expanded: Differences in hemoglobin measurement or correction method limit attribution of the DLCO change to pulmonary disease.

templates.standard: The compared studies were obtained in different bronchodilator states.
templates.expanded: A comparison between pre- and post-bronchodilator measurements may reflect treatment state as well as longitudinal physiology.

templates.concise: A reduced FEV1/FVC is newly demonstrated.
templates.standard: FEV1/FVC is now below the LLN on comparable testing.
templates.expanded: A newly reduced ratio is demonstrated; review proximity to the LLN and test quality before assigning clinical significance.

templates.standard: TLC is now below the LLN on reliable comparable testing.
templates.expanded: A new restrictive ventilatory impairment is supported by the low TLC; the underlying cause requires clinical assessment.

templates.concise: FVC change meets the PPF physiologic threshold.
templates.standard: The comparable FVC decline meets the FVC component of the PPF physiologic criterion.
templates.expanded: In the documented non-IPF fibrotic ILD setting and time window, the FVC decline meets a physiologic PPF threshold; a full PPF determination requires the other guideline domains and exclusion of alternative explanations.

templates.concise: DLCO change meets the PPF physiologic threshold.
templates.standard: The comparable hemoglobin-adjusted DLCO decline meets the DLCO component of the PPF physiologic criterion.
