templates.expanded: In the documented non-IPF fibrotic ILD setting and time window, the DLCO decline meets a physiologic PPF threshold; this alone does not establish PPF and alternative causes of a DLCO decline must be considered.

templates.concise: Normal spirometry, lung volumes, and DLCO.
templates.standard: Spirometry, lung volumes, and diffusing capacity are within reference limits.
templates.expanded: The tested routine pulmonary-function domains are within reference limits; this does not exclude disease outside the sensitivity or scope of these tests.

templates.standard: The available spirometric measurements are within reference limits.
templates.expanded: Spirometry is normal; a statement of normal complete pulmonary function is not supported without the other requested test domains.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is present with diffusing capacity within reference limits.
templates.expanded: Airflow obstruction is demonstrated without a measured gas-transfer deficit; this physiology alone does not distinguish asthma from other airway disorders.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is accompanied by reduced diffusing capacity.
templates.expanded: The combined findings show airflow limitation and gas-transfer impairment; a specific cause requires imaging and clinical correlation.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is accompanied by an air-trapping lung-volume pattern.
templates.expanded: Spirometry and volume distribution show airflow limitation with retained residual volume; the mechanism is not specific to one airway diagnosis.

templates.standard: An obstructive ventilatory impairment is accompanied by a hyperinflation volume pattern.
templates.expanded: Both airflow limitation and increased resting or residual-volume fractions are demonstrated.

templates.standard: A restrictive ventilatory impairment is present with DLCO within reference limits.
templates.expanded: Restriction is confirmed without a measured gas-transfer deficit; preserved DLCO does not independently establish an extrapulmonary cause.

templates.standard: A restrictive ventilatory impairment is accompanied by a gas-transfer deficit.
templates.expanded: The combined restrictive and diffusion abnormalities are compatible with several processes, including parenchymal disease, but do not establish ILD.

templates.standard: Mixed obstructive and restrictive impairment is accompanied by a gas-transfer deficit.
templates.expanded: Reliable spirometry and TLC support mixed impairment, with an additional reduction in measured gas transfer.

templates.standard: Reduced spirometric volumes with preserved ratio and normal TLC are accompanied by low DLCO.
templates.expanded: A nonspecific ventilatory pattern and gas-transfer deficit are present; the combined findings warrant clinical correlation rather than a spirometry-only diagnosis of restriction.

templates.concise: Preserved spirometry and lung volumes with reduced DLCO.
templates.standard: The only demonstrated routine functional abnormality is reduced diffusing capacity.
templates.expanded: A gas-transfer deficit is present despite preserved spirometry and volumes; technical and clinical contributors should be assessed.

templates.concise: The pattern is compatible with emphysema in the appropriate setting.
templates.standard: Obstruction, hyperinflation, and reduced DLCO may support emphysema physiology.
templates.expanded: The combination is compatible with emphysema when supported by imaging and clinical history; the PFT pattern alone does not confirm the diagnosis.

templates.concise: An extrapulmonary contribution to restriction is possible.
templates.standard: The restrictive pattern with relatively preserved transfer findings may reflect reduced lung expansion.
templates.expanded: Body habitus, chest-wall mechanics, or respiratory muscle dysfunction may contribute in the appropriate setting; PFTs alone do not distinguish these from every parenchymal process.

templates.concise: A parenchymal contribution to restriction is possible.
templates.standard: Restriction with impaired gas transfer may reflect parenchymal lung disease.
templates.expanded: The findings can support concern for parenchymal disease when concordant with imaging and history; pulmonary vascular, hemoglobin, and technical contributors may also affect DLCO.

phrases.label: Obtain volumes to assess low FVC

templates.concise: Consider lung volumes to assess for restriction.
templates.standard: Lung-volume measurement may clarify the reduced FVC.
templates.expanded: If clinically indicated, reliable TLC measurement can distinguish restriction from other causes of reduced vital capacity.

templates.concise: Consider repeat testing if clinically useful.
templates.standard: Repeat testing may improve confidence if the result will affect care.
templates.expanded: A repeat study with improved maneuver quality may clarify the pattern or its severity if this information is clinically consequential.

templates.standard: A current hemoglobin and the laboratory adjustment method may clarify the gas-transfer finding.
templates.expanded: If anemia or a change in hemoglobin is clinically relevant, a consistent hemoglobin-adjusted comparison may improve interpretation.

templates.standard: Reproducible central-airway loop abnormalities may warrant additional evaluation.
templates.expanded: Persistent, reproducible loop flattening should be correlated with symptoms and, when appropriate, anatomic or laryngeal assessment.

templates.standard: Repeat or complementary respiratory muscle testing may clarify the low pressure values.
templates.expanded: If the clinical concern persists, complementary testing may help distinguish true muscle dysfunction from limitations of volitional mouth-pressure measurements.

templates.concise: Consider bronchial challenge if clinically indicated.
templates.standard: A normal spirometric study may be followed by bronchial challenge when the diagnostic question warrants it.
templates.expanded: Bronchial challenge can be considered within an appropriate clinical assessment when variable airway disease remains a concern despite nondiagnostic spirometry.

templates.standard: Interpret these physiologic findings alongside symptoms, exposures, and relevant imaging.
templates.expanded: The PFT describes measured physiology; the clinical diagnosis requires integration with the relevant history and other investigations.
